title: Artificial_intimacy
summary:
Artificial intimacy is a form of human-AI interaction in which an individual forms social connections, emotional bonds, or intimate relationships with various forms of artificial intelligence, including chatbots, virtual assistants, and other artificial entities.

The interpersonal model of intimacy considers communication to be key in affiliative bonding, suggesting that intimacy develops and deepens through open communication between partners. Specifically, when individuals communicate emotions and perceive their partner as responsive and caring, feelings of closeness and connection are enhanced, building intimacy. Artificial entities are able to mimic interpersonal communication between humans, which can simulate sensations of intimacy within human users through a perceived sense of responsiveness. The relationship between human and AI does not come with the cost of vulnerability or social rejection, which may make self-disclosure easier than with other humans.

Research by Skjuve et al on Replika chatbot users found that users' perception of chatbots as "accepting, understanding and non-judgmental" facilitated relationship development between the AI and users. Xie et al's study found loneliness to be a driving factor in chatbot interaction. Herbener and Damholdt's study on Danish high school students found that students who sought emotional support or engaged in reciprocal conversations with chatbots were significantly more lonely than their peers and used the chatbots to cope with negative emotions.

Overall, the evidence suggests an innate need for bonding evokes feelings of loneliness in users, who turn to artificial intimacy as a low-cost method to alleviate these emotions. However, some researchers caution that pursuing artificial intimacy may lead to reduced social motivation, social substitution effects, withdrawal from real-life relationships, and difficulty discerning reality from fantasy, which may increase longer-term loneliness and isolation.
